failureModes.prompt: If someone taps pay twice, or the network retries, should they be charged once or twice?
failureModes.why: a double charge is the most damaging bug this feature can have

options.label: Charge once
options.consequence: needs a stable id per attempt

options.label: Charge per request
options.consequence: simplest, and people get charged twice

failureModes.provenBy: a test that submits the same payment twice and asserts exactly one charge exists

failureModes.prompt: If the app closes between paying and our server hearing about it, what should happen?
failureModes.why: money can move without our records knowing

options.label: Reconcile from the provider
options.consequence: always correct, needs a background check

options.label: Trust the app to report back
options.consequence: simplest, and paid people can end up locked out

failureModes.provenBy: a test that drops the confirmation callback and asserts reconciliation still grants the purchase

failureModes.prompt: What should decide whether someone has access — the phone or the server?
failureModes.why: it decides whether access can be faked on a modified device

options.label: The server
options.consequence: trustworthy, needs a check before paid features

failureModes.provenBy: a test that grants access on the server and asserts a modified client cannot grant itself access

failureModes.prompt: When a renewal fails, should access stop immediately or continue for a grace period?
failureModes.why: cards fail routinely for reasons that are nobody's fault

options.label: Grace period
options.consequence: keeps good customers, briefly gives away access

options.label: Stop immediately
options.consequence: no leakage, punishes an expired card

failureModes.provenBy: a test that fails a renewal and asserts access follows the chosen policy (grace, or immediate stop)
